titles.487: Annotatio IV §.II open: Cosinus mentions John 6 and Paul as mode-commentaries
titles.488: Annotatio IV §.II: Institution shows presence and participation — special Mode from Christ & Paul
titles.489: Annotatio IV §.II: Dispute on John 6 — is it about the Lord’s Supper? Both sides true
titles.490: Annotatio IV §.II cont.: Not full (no bread/wine) but semi-full (flesh eaten / blood drunk)
titles.491: Annotatio IV §.II: John 6 = antecedent most lucid commentary on the Institution words
titles.492: Annotatio IV §.II close: Mode merely Spiritual / Supernatural / Celestial — stop before §.III

latin.487: §. II. Oportunè admodum Doctiss. Episcopus cùm Sermonis Christi de manducanda carne sua, & bibendo sanguine suo Joh. 6. tum Sermonis Paulini, de panis & poculi Eucharisticorum communione cum corpore & sanguine Christi, mentionem hôc locô injicit.
latin.488: Quandoquidem etiam Institutionis S. Cœnæ verba corporis & sanguinis Christi tùm præsentiam, tum participationem satis distinctè insinuant, de Modo tamen utriusque speciali decernunt nihil, ut hic totus ex dictis Christi & Pauli sermonibus, ceu unicis quidem sed plenissimis ac luculentissimis Commentariis, petendus ac addiscendus veniat.
latin.489: Equidem de Joh. 6., id diu satis & acriter disceptatum est, etiam inter ejusdem Sectæ Christianæ Theologos: Num in eo, de Cœna Domini, de præsentia & manducatione carnis & bibitione sanguinis Christi Sacramentalibus agatur? Aliis affirmativam, negativam aliis, tenentibus magnoque tuentibus conatu. At litigium istud facilè ita componitur, ut utraque pars verum dixisse intelligatur.
latin.490: Enimverò de Cœna S. deque præsentia & manducatione corporis ac bibitione sanguinis Christi sacramentalibus, agitur alicubi, vel plenè & quà totum horum, vel semiplenè & qua partem aliquam. Priori modo de Cœna deque præsentia & participatione corporis & sanguinis Christi sacramentalibus, ditô loco non agi, in propatulo est, quia non agitur de pane & vino Eucharisticis, nec de horum vel præsentia, vel participatione, quæ interim Sacramenti S. Cœnæ nec non sacramentalis præsentiæ ac participationis partes integrantes, quin essentiales, constituunt; at posteriori modo de iisdem agi, non minus in aprico est, quia agitur de manducatione carnis & bibitione sanguinis Christi, eòque tùm de præcipuo S. Cœnæ & proprio & proximo Objecto, carne & sanguine Christi, tum de præcipua eaque sacramentali, Sacræ Cœnæ celebrationis imperata à Christo actione, scil. manducatione corporis & bibitione sanguinis ejus.
latin.491: Ceterum hôc posteriori modo cap. Joh. 6. de S. Cœna deque Sacramentali & carnis & sanguinis Christi tùm præsentia, tùm participatione, ita specialtim agitur, ut quis hic modus sacramentalis utriusque, & qualis censendus sit, omnium disertissimè inibi exponatur, quô proinde nomine sermonem Christi, Joh. 6. cap. habitum, antecedaneum verborum Institutionis Christi eumque luculentissimum Commentarium arbitramur esse, i. e. Commentarium non de jam tum instituta, sed de paulò post instituenda S. Cœna, tantam huic facem præferentem, tantumque luminis, concisis Institutionis Christi verbis: Hoc est Corpus meum, & Hic enim sanguis meus, fæneratum, ut Discipulis Christi, per Magistri sui sermonem istum, objectionibus & dubiis suis omnibus plenissimè liberatis, nullum amplius scrupulum ista vel moverint, vel quiverint movere.
latin.492: Est verò hic Modus tàm præsentiæ, quàm participationis carnis & sanguinis Christi, mere Spiritualis, Supernaturalis, Cælestis, corporali, naturali, carnali localique, ceu vel magis, vel minus Capernaitico, oppositus.

pass_a.487: §. II. Most opportunely the Most Learned Bishop here injects mention both of Christ’s discourse on eating His flesh and drinking His blood in John 6, and of Paul’s discourse on the communion of the Eucharistic bread and cup with the body and blood of Christ.
pass_a.488: Since even the words of the Institution of the Sacred Supper sufficiently distinctly insinuate both the presence and the participation of Christ’s body and blood, yet decide nothing about the special Mode of either, so that this whole Mode is to be sought and learned from the said discourses of Christ and Paul, as the only but fullest and most lucid Commentaries.
pass_a.489: Indeed concerning John 6, it has long enough and sharply been disputed, even among theologians of the same Christian sect: Whether in it there is discourse of the Lord’s Supper, of the sacramental presence and eating of flesh and drinking of Christ’s blood? Some holding the affirmative, others the negative, and defending with great effort. But that lawsuit is easily so composed that each side is understood to have spoken truth.
pass_a.490: For concerning the Sacred Supper and the sacramental presence and eating of the body and drinking of Christ’s blood, discourse is held somewhere either fully and as to the whole of these, or semi-fully and as to some part. In the former way it is open that at that place there is no discourse of the Supper and of sacramental presence and participation of Christ’s body and blood, because there is no discourse of Eucharistic bread and wine, nor of their presence or participation, which meanwhile constitute the integrating, even essential, parts of the Sacrament of the Sacred Supper and of sacramental presence and participation; but in the latter way it is no less clear that there is discourse of the same, because there is discourse of eating flesh and drinking Christ’s blood, and thus both of the chief and proper and nearest Object of the Sacred Supper, Christ’s flesh and blood, and of the chief and sacramental action of celebrating the Sacred Supper commanded by Christ, namely eating His body and drinking His blood.
pass_a.491: Moreover in this latter way John 6 treats so specially of the Sacred Supper and of the sacramental presence and participation of Christ’s flesh and blood, that what this sacramental Mode of either is, and of what sort it is to be judged, is there set out most expressly of all; wherefore we judge Christ’s discourse held in John 6 to be the antecedent and most lucid Commentary on Christ’s Institution words — i.e. a Commentary not on the Supper already then instituted, but on the Sacred Supper shortly to be instituted, holding so great a torch to it, and lending so much light to the concise Institution words This is my Body, and For this is my blood, that Christ’s disciples, fully freed from all their objections and doubts by that discourse of their Master, those words either moved or could move no further scruple.
pass_a.492: But this Mode both of presence and of participation of Christ’s flesh and blood is merely Spiritual, Supernatural, Celestial, opposed to the corporal, natural, carnal and local — whether more or less Capernaite.

487: §.II: Cosinus (Most Learned Bishop) aptly brings in two discourses here.
John 6 — eating Christ’s flesh and drinking His blood; and Paul — communion of Eucharistic bread and cup with Christ’s body and blood.
488: Institution words clearly enough hint presence and participation of body and blood — but decide nothing about the special Mode of either.
That whole Mode must be sought from Christ’s and Paul’s discourses as the only, fullest, most lucid commentaries.
489: Long sharp fight even within the same Christian camp: does John 6 treat the Lord’s Supper and sacramental eating/drinking of Christ’s flesh and blood?
Some yes, some no — both sides can be true once the dispute is composed.
490: Supper-talk can be full (the whole) or semi-full (a part). John 6 is not full: no Eucharistic bread and wine, which are essential integrating parts of the sacrament.
It is semi-full: it does treat eating flesh and drinking blood — the Supper’s chief nearest object and the commanded sacramental action.
491: So read, John 6 specially exposes what the sacramental Mode of presence and participation is — the antecedent, most lucid commentary on the Institution words.
Not on a Supper already instituted then, but on the one soon to be: torch and light for ‘This is my Body’ / ‘This is my blood,’ clearing the disciples’ scruples.
492: That Mode of presence and participation is merely Spiritual, Supernatural, Celestial.
It stands against corporal, natural, carnal, local presence — Capernaite in greater or lesser degree.
Stop before §.III (four proofs that John 6 inculcates the spiritual mode).

notes.488: Mode not in Institution; from commentaries.
notes.490: Full vs semi-full; bread/wine vs flesh/blood.
